name: Question 13
problem:
Evaluate the triple integral

$$
{∭}_{R}20y\,\text{d}V
$$

where $R$ is the type III region given by 

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le z\le 1-{x}^{2},\,0\le y\le 1-x}.
$$
worked_solution:
Writing down our triple integral as a repeated integral, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}2x\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-{x}^{2}}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}20y\,dy\,dz\,dx.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y$, treating $x$ and $z$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-{x}^{2}}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}20y\,dy\,dz\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-{x}^{2}}[{\int }_{0}^{1-x}20y\,dy]dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-{x}^{2}}[10{y}^{2}]_{y=0}^{y=1-x}dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-{x}^{2}}10(1-x)^{2}\,dz\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z$, treating $x$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-{x}^{2}}10(1-x)^{2}\,dz\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{1-{x}^{2}}10(1-x)^{2}\,dz]dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}10(1-x)^{2}[z]_{z=0}^{z=1-{x}^{2}}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}10(1-x)^{2}(1-{x}^{2})dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}10(1-2x+2{x}^{3}-{x}^{4})\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}10(1-2x+2{x}^{3}-{x}^{4})\,dx & ={[10(x-{x}^{2}+\frac{{x}^{4}}{2}-\frac{{x}^{5}}{5})]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

Writing down our triple integral as a repeated integral, we obtain

∭R2xdV=∫01∫01−x2∫01−x20ydydzdx.

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to y, treating x and z as constants:

∫01∫01−x2∫01−x20ydydzdx=∫01∫01−x2[∫01−x20ydy]dzdx=∫01∫01−x2[10y2]y=0y=1−xdzdx=∫01∫01−x210(1−x)2dzdx

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to z, treating x as a constant:

∫01∫01−x210(1−x)2dzdx=∫01[∫01−x210(1−x)2dz]dx=∫0110(1−x)2[z]z=0z=1−x2dx=∫0110(1−x)2(1−x2)dx=∫0110(1−2x+2x3−x4)dx

Finally, we integrate with respect to x:

∫0110(1−2x+2x3−x4)dx=[10(x−x2+x42−x55)]x=0x=1=3.
